sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Mailchimp, now presented under the Intuit brand, sells email and SMS marketing with AI and automation to small and growing businesses, with industry pages for restaurants, ecommerce, nonprofits and more.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'Turn ideas into emails & SMS that connect', with an Intuit Intelligence line about winning back customers who've gone quiet.
A banner offers a free 14-day trial or 15% off on 10,000+ contacts.
The homepage names a competitor: 'Save up to 42% by switching from Klaviyo to Mailchimp*'.
Industry pages such as the restaurants page repeat the unified email and SMS pitch in each trade's terms.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: An email and SMS marketing suite with AI content tools, automation and a large integration catalog.

rows: Campaigns, templates, an email builder, A/B testing and popup forms
Texting alongside email, with consent and compliance
Behavior-based triggers; customers see up to 8x more orders with flows, by Mailchimp's claim
Generative AI features, Content Studio and dynamic content
Landing pages and social media marketing
A separate API product for developers
300+ apps including Shopify, WooCommerce, Square, Stripe and Canva

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Priced by contact count, with a free plan, a 14-day free trial of the Standard plan and paid tiers from $20 a month. The page is a configurator, so most prices appear only after you choose a contact tier.
keyPoints: 'Under 250 contacts? It's free.'
Standard is the lead plan: free for 14 days, then from $20 a month, sending up to 6,000 emails a month at the lowest contact tier.
A contacts menu steps from 0-500 up to 1,000,000+; a 15% discount applies from 10,000+ contacts.
Overages apply if the contact or email-send limit is exceeded, and the page notes a 'Find the right plan' recommendation flow and nonprofit rates.

rows: A cheaper step down from Standard; price depends on contacts
Free for 14 days, then from $20 a month; generative AI, enhanced automations, custom-coded templates, popup forms, personalized onboarding
Higher tier for large senders; price depends on contacts

gaps: Essentials and Premium prices were not on the page text; a currency selector and the contact configurator hide most prices.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: A configurator-led ladder that leads with the middle plan on a free trial and lets visitors downgrade later. Promotions are used heavily, including against a named competitor.
keyPoints: Standard is the default offer: 'Try our Standard plan for free!', with a note that you can downgrade to Essentials or Free at any time.
A contact-tier menu, a currency selector, a 'Find the right plan' flow and a 15% volume discount make the price list interactive.
A switch offer ('Save up to 42% by switching from Klaviyo') targets a rival's customers.
For merchants: automation flows, A/B testing, dynamic content, SMS and email together, landing pages and 300+ integrations.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A developer section covers the Marketing API and Transactional API with release notes, and the docs advertise a machine-readable index for AI agents.
keyPoints: A public changelog lists API changes for Transactional and the Marketing API, including new Audiences endpoints in beta and a longer webhook retry interval.
A line on the page tells AI agents that a documentation index is available at /llms.txt, with a markdown version of each page.
The integrations directory has 300+ apps, filterable, including a developer-tools category.
gaps: API reference and rate limits were not read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Warm and friendly: a rounded serif display, a signature yellow and dark brown, pill buttons and a photographic hero. The signup and developer pages use different styles.
keyPoints: Marketing pages use Means Web with yellow (#ffe01b) and dark brown (#231e15) and 26px button corners.
The home hero is a darkened photograph with a white headline and an italic yellow 'that connect', with a star rating and review-site logos below.
The pricing page puts a white Standard plan card with a contact-tier menu at the right of a headline and a checklist.
The signup page switches to Graphik Web with teal (#017e89) and 38px corners, and the developer release notes use teal-blue with 8px corners.
A strip of Intuit brand links (TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp) sits above the header.
The home page is 8,340px tall.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A scale and ratings story, now under the Intuit umbrella, with big numbers that differ from page to page.
keyPoints: Homepage: customers generated $1.1 billion in gross revenue in 62 days, with a rating based on 33,000+ reviews.
The pricing page says customers see up to 27x ROI; the content-tools page says up to 30x.
The content-tools page claims 11M+ users and more than 99% deliverability.
Success stories include Budget Atlanta's 4x open rates from segmentation.
gaps: No leadership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: From the homepage 'Start Free Trial' goes to the pricing page, where the plan card's own 'Start Free Trial' and a 'Sign Up' button lead on, three clicks in total, to login.mailchimp.com/signup headed 'Start with Mailchimp for Free'. It is a real account form asking language, business email, username and password, with a line saying you agree to the Terms and have read the Global Privacy Statement. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Every page is about reaching customers by email and SMS; industry pages name the trade.

capability_visible.evidence: Features pages, an interactive product tour and a free plan show a lot; the app itself is behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Free, and 'from $20' for Standard are clear; other prices appear only after choosing a contact tier.

product_breadth.evidence: Email, SMS, flows, AI tools, landing pages and transactional are each explained.

platform_depth.evidence: Marketing and Transactional APIs with a public changelog and an llms.txt index.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: The trial path takes three clicks and ends at a form asking language, business email, username and password.

trust.evidence: A rating based on 33,000+ reviews, review-site logos and case studies with numbers.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'Turn ideas into emails and SMS that connect' is clear about the channels.

proof_quality.evidence: ROI claims carry asterisks and differ across pages (27x vs 30x); revenue and rating figures are not sourced on the page.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: A '42% switch from Klaviyo' offer has an asterisk; trial terms are linked but long.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Start Free Trial' is the one consistent primary action, with 'Get a demo' beside it.

company_narrative.evidence: The email-and-SMS-with-AI story holds across pages; the Intuit framing is added on top.

offer_packaging.evidence: Four plans with a configurator and clear lead plan; prices beyond the lowest tier are hidden.

offer_architecture.evidence: Free tier, a 14-day trial of the middle plan, a downgrade path, a volume discount and a competitor-switch offer.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Automation flows, A/B testing, dynamic content, SMS plus email and landing pages; no catalogue tools.

visual_craft.evidence: Warm, legible hierarchy with a distinctive yellow; busy top bars.

system_coherence.evidence: Marketing, signup and developer pages use different fonts, colors and button shapes.

merchant_design_control.evidence: Branded templates, custom-coded email templates, popup forms and a Canva integration.

read.summary: A mature email and SMS platform with a trial-first, configurator-led pricing page and a lot of promotional energy, including an offer aimed at a named competitor. Proof numbers are large but unsourced and inconsistent between pages.
pros: A free plan and a 14-day trial of the middle plan lower the entry bar.
A public API changelog and an llms.txt index.
Many merchant tools: flows, A/B tests, SMS plus email and landing pages.
Case studies and a ratings count add proof.
cons: Most prices appear only after choosing a contact tier.
ROI claims differ between pages (27x and 30x) and carry asterisks.
The trial path takes three clicks and a long form.
Signup, marketing and developer pages look like different products.
read.howItSells: Sells approachability and results: a friendly brand, a free start, big revenue and ROI numbers, and a direct switch offer against a competitor.
copy: Make a trial of the middle plan the default offer.
Let visitors downgrade later and say so.
Use a configurator for contact-based pricing.
avoid: ROI numbers that change from page to page.
A form that asks for username as well as email.
unknowns: Prices above the lowest contact tier.
What the trial includes in practice.

hypothesis.statement: Showing a plain price table for the first three contact tiers next to the configurator will raise trial starts among visitors who leave before choosing a tier.
hypothesis.guardrail: Plan-change and support contacts about billing
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if trial starts rise by a pre-agreed margin and billing contacts do not rise over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: A trial-first ladder with a heavy use of promotions, strongest on merchant tools and weakest on showing prices.
pros: Free plan plus a trial of the middle plan.

design.summary: Friendly and distinctive on the marketing site, with a clear seam at signup and the developer pages.
pros: A recognisable yellow and a warm serif give personality.
The pricing page puts one plan card next to a clear promise.
cons: Signup and developer pages switch fonts and colors.
Two stacked top bars before the page starts.
